site.name: dew
site.tagline: A desktop synth DAW where the song can be written as text.
site.status: Working prototype. Every layer is real and wired to the next. macOS only.

home.intro: A channel rack with a step grid, a piano roll, a playlist of clips and a mixer, driven by a three-oscillator synth per channel — or by a recording, or by a song written as text and compiled to notes.
home.tabsBody: The same notes, seen four ways, and a fifth tab that writes them for you.

features.title: What it does
features.lead: Each of these is built and wired to the next. Nothing here is a mock.

design.title: Design system
design.lead: One vocabulary, held to a number rather than to taste. Every value on this page is read out of the application's own tokens.
design.coloursBody: Named for their role, never their appearance. A theme is one assignment because each name is a reference into the palette in force.
design.rampBody: Not themeable. These eight are document data, written into every project file, so repainting them would make a saved project disagree with the swatch it was chosen from.
design.liftBody: How much lighter a surface gets when touched. A large surface needs a subtler lift than a small one — that distinction is real, and the other values that had grown beside it were not.
design.galleryCaption: The whole design system on one page, rendered by dew_shot gallery.

score.title: The score language
score.lead: A song written as text and compiled to real patterns, notes and clips. Seven block keywords, and the set is closed.
score.exampleCaption: examples/amber.score — the one CI compiles and renders.
score.noExpressions: There is no expression language — no arithmetic, no variables, no conditionals. That single restriction is what makes completion a table lookup rather than type inference, and what lets the grid be computed statically before anything is generated.

reference.title: Score language reference
reference.lead: Generated from the same table the compiler validates against and the editor completes from, so a key cannot be documented differently from how it is checked.
reference.noKeys: A list body rather than a set of keys.
